zh.chartTitle: 某防癌筛查机构海报：「早发现，让五年生存率提升 50%！」附两组数据（单位：%）。海报没提的是，筛查也会查出许多终生不会发病的结节。

textRefs.debunk_survival: 「五年生存率提升 50%」是相对说法：从 2% 涨到 3%，绝对值只多了 1 个百分点。相对值听着惊天动地，绝对值才决定它到底意味着什么。
textRefs.debunk_overdiag: 筛查组「年检出」80 远高于不筛查组 50——多出来的，大多是终生不会发病、却被提前贴上「病人」标签的过度诊断（lead-time bias）。存活曲线变长，可能只是更早被记录，而非真的多活了几年。

manual: 这个「50%」到底在比什么？两个数差多少，才配叫「提升一半」？
筛查多找出的病例，是治好了更多人，还是只是更早发现了原本无害的东西？
zh.explanation: 这张海报玩了两个文字游戏：①「提升 50%」是相对值（2%→3%），绝对值只多 1 个百分点，听起来天差地别实则微乎其微；②筛查多检出的，很多是终生无害的结节（过度诊断），存活率变长可能只是 lead-time bias——更早被记录，不是更被治愈。看任何「生存率暴涨」先问：是相对还是绝对？多查出的，是救了还是吓到了？

en.chartTitle: A cancer-screening poster: 'Early detection raised 5-year survival by 50%!' with two data sets (unit: %). What the poster omits: screening also finds many nodules that would never become disease.

textRefs.debunk_survival: '5-year survival up 50%' is a relative claim: from 2% to 3%, the absolute gain is just 1 percentage point. Relative numbers sound earth-shaking; the absolute number decides what it actually means.
textRefs.debunk_overdiag: The screened group's 'found per year' is 80 vs 50 unscreened — most of the excess are over-diagnosed nodules that would never cause disease yet get labeled 'patient' early (lead-time bias). A longer survival curve may just mean earlier recording, not more years truly lived.

manual: What exactly is this '50%' comparing? How big a gap between two numbers earns the words 'half again'?
Did screening find and cure more people, or merely spot harmless things earlier?
en.explanation: This poster plays two word games: ① 'up 50%' is relative (2%→3%), an absolute gain of just 1 point — sounds monumental, means little; ② much of what screening finds is harmless nodules (over-diagnosis), and a longer survival curve may be lead-time bias — recorded earlier, not truly cured longer. With any 'survival surge', ask: relative or absolute? Did finding more save more, or just scare more?
